requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.

Where an ESA is (part of) a light source, the ESA shall either hold an approval according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128, or be not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
Every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10 shall bear an approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3.
The ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The ESA(s) shall meet the requirements for radiated emissions.
The ESA(s) shall meet the requirements for conducted emissions.
The ESA(s) shall meet the requirements for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The ESA(s) shall meet the requirements for immunity to conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall comply with the limits when measured by the method described in Annex 7.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
For measurements made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9 with the test severity given in Table 2a in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and with the minimum test level given in Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the stripline method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range and a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

For the TEM cell method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range and a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency range.

For the BCI method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range and a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

For the ALSE method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range.

For the ALSE method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range and a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.

For the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range.

For the reverberation chamber method, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range and a minimum test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The ESA starting profile immunity shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the ESA for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall be tested with the starting profile at immunity test level II for 12 V systems and II for 24 V systems with 10 pulses, achieving functional status B for immunity related functions of ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases, C for immunity related functions of other ESA, and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 1, the ESA shall withstand -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC III for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall withstand +37 V (12 V system) or +37 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall withstand +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses with FPSC II for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall withstand -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall withstand +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9.

ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband electromagnetic emission test.
The ESA under test for narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that these result in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9 being covered, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA immunity test conditions shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
The ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
Conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited.

Where two or more lamps are part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions set out in this Regulation or in another Regulation.
Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The value for "a" with regard to the size of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall, in the case where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).

Lamps with an electronic light source control gear and/or a variable luminous intensity control and/or a secondary operating mode and/or non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
The specific identification code of the replaceable light source module shall comprise the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed.
Where several non-identical light source modules are used, the approval mark shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
The approval mark on the light source module shall be from the same applicant as the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used.
The light source module shall be marked with the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
The lamp shall be marked with the specific identification code of the light source module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
The lamp shall be marked with the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
Where an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a) shall be affixed on the component.

The size of the components of a single approval mark of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN Regulation No. 148.

The lamp shall comply with the requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval.

The lamp shall meet the requirements of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 that are pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 148.

A rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, using a common light source and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source) or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

Where the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates a manufacturer logo, it shall incorporate only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components, and all requirements for the specific function of UN Regulation No. 148 shall be fulfilled.

Where a lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be allowed.

Where a lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following provisions shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and, when all light sources are illuminated, the maximum intensities are not exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced, in which case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum value of category S3, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
Light signalling devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device are met.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of different positions, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined, except for rear-registration plate illuminating lamps.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The luminous intensity of the lamp shall observe the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.
The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the limits specified for the pertinent function.
The compliance of the luminous intensities of the lamp shall be verified by tests carried out according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted shall comply with the colorimetric characteristics inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, checked with the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted shall be observed.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.

The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear position lamp or rear end-outline marker lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 4.

A luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp or rear end-outline marker lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the stop lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the reversing lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 10.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied.
Where the type approval of the reversing lamp is granted applying the pair-only condition, the device shall only be installed in a pair.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
Lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under this Regulation.

Unless specified otherwise, the luminous intensity of the lamp in the various directions of measurement shall be not less than the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with the direction H = 0° and V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference.

Where front and rear direction indicator lamps, front and rear position lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, parking lamps, stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS, or side marker lamps are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity of the lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

For reversing lamps, if visual examination of the lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by the lamp shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
Mass-produced lamps shall not differ from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations.

When the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation are tested on any mass-produced lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates of the lamp shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.

The lamp shall withstand a one-hour test of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C, with a light source of the category specified for the lamp supplied with a current at a voltage such that it gives the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources (filament light sources and other), the heat resistance test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with paragraph 5.4.5. of this Regulation.
Where only the maximum power is specified, the heat resistance test of the lamp shall be carried out by regulating the voltage to obtain a power equal to 90 per cent of the specified power.
The specified average or maximum power for the heat resistance test shall in all cases be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value.
For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the heat resistance test conditions set in paragraph 5.4.5. or 5.9.5. of this Regulation shall be applied.

In the case of light sources operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity, the heat resistance test shall be carried out under the conditions given at minimum 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity.
After the lamp has been stabilized at the ambient temperature following the heat resistance test, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification shall be perceptible.

In case of doubt, the intensity of light of the lamp measured according to paragraph 5. of this Regulation shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.

For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For lamps (functions) other than reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
The device shall be marked with the approval number assigned to its type, following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.

Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
Where the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown in UN R150 paragraph 3.3.3.1.
Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

A retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.

Where lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated in retroreflective devices, the size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Retro-reflectors approved under UN R150 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The retro-reflecting device shall meet the requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval.

The requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed shall be applied to the retro-reflecting device, where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough.
Any protuberances the outer surface of retro-reflective devices may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
Where a retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflective device, when illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.), shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

Retro-reflectors of the Classes IA and IB shall, at least one hour after the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6, meet the colorimetric characteristics of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI of paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
Retro-reflectors of the Classes IA and IB shall withstand the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) followed by the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

Retro-reflectors of the Classes IA and IB shall, if necessary, withstand the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6 followed by the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
Retro-reflectors of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
Retro-reflectors of the Classes IA and IB shall withstand the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors of the Classes IA and IB in each group shall have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

For photometric measurements of Class IA or IB retro-reflective devices, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.
The illuminating surface of the Class IA or IB retro-reflective device shall be limited to 100 cm2, though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

The RI values for Class IA and Class IB red retro-reflectors, when measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

For retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP", the RI in the position of minimum RI, obtained by rotating the device about its axis of reference with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.

For retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP", the RI measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, with the device placed in the position corresponding to the value of ε of minimum RI, shall attain the specified values, where the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position if the specified values are not attained.

For retro-reflective devices marked "TOP", the RI shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during rotation about its axis of ±5° with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20'.

For moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall withstand being kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.

The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface of the water.

The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall withstand a repeat of the 10-minute immersion in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C after being turned through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall withstand being immediately immersed afterwards in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water on the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the moisture and dust tests.
Upon completion of the drain period following the water spray test, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the device.
Upon completion of the drain period following the water spray test, no standing pool of water shall be able to be formed in the interior of the device by tapping or tilting the device.
The retro-reflector shall resist dust penetration which could significantly affect its photometric output when exposed to test dust of fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
All drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open during the dust exposure test.

The retro-reflective device shall resist dust penetration when exposed for a duration of 5 hours to test dust agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s, with the dust allowed to settle between the agitation periods.

Retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The front surface of the retro-reflective device shall resist tarnishing and the protection of the rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly where an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked, when tested for resistance to corrosion as described in ISO Standard 9227:2017.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

Retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
Samples of retro-reflective devices shall withstand exposure in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013, using the parameters given in Table A6-1, for a period of 500 hours.

The accelerated artificial weathering exposure of the samples shall use either method TM1 (black-standard thermometer, cycle No. 1 according to EN ISO 4892-2:2013: 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, broadband irradiance (300 to 400 nm) 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband irradiance (340 nm) 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², black-standard temperature 65 ± 3 °C, relative humidity 50 ± 10 per cent) or method TM2 (black-panel thermometer, cycle No. 4 according to EN ISO 4892-2:2013: 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, broadband irradiance (300 to 400 nm) 60 ± 2 W/m², narrowband irradiance (340 nm) 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², black-panel temperature 63 ± 3 °C, relative humidity 50 ± 10 per cent).

The outer surface of the retro-reflective device, and in particular the illuminating surface, shall not show any apparent surface changes, except slight surface cracks, when inspected visually about five minutes after being lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.

For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangles of type 1, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation after the outer surface, and in particular the illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil and then cleaned after about 5 minutes.
The approval number on the retro-reflective device shall be placed close to the circle surrounding the letter "E", in any position in relation to it.
The digits constituting the approval number on the retro-reflective device shall face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflective device shall be placed diametrically opposite the approval number.
The method used to determine the apparent surface shall be declared for each lamp, as defined in paragraph 2.5., and recorded in item 10.2. of Annex 1.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For all signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of light-signalling devices laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall comply with the requirements when verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, in the case where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the general requirements for the fitting of lamps shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extending on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
The illumination of the surface of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

Where the light-emitting surface of lamps in the shape of a band or strip is constituted by a number of juxtaposed elements, these individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
The maximum height above the ground of a lamp shall be determined from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

With the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

With the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirements on no direct visibility of red light to the front and white light to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.

Where the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1. shall be satisfied.

Where the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), additional lamps for these functions switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

Where the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, with the exception of direction indicator lamps, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with UN R48.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position (stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not) different from the "normal position of use", unless this is not practicable and the alternative provisions apply.

Where the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps or retro-reflectors is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for these lamps shall be switched ON, as one of the permitted alternatives.
Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
The replacement device providing a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function shall remain operational in its original safety function.

During temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of UN R48) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

Where rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., the intensity of all these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

Where rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions in the entire intensity range.

Rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control shall show no sharp variation of intensity during transition.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, except that no account is taken of obstacles if they were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device, and proof thereof shall be furnished.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN Regulation No. 48 when installed on a vehicle.
The reversing lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The number of stop lamps shall be two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device on all categories of vehicles.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the height above the ground shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

If the optional S1 or S2 category stop lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except for the optional rear lamps.

The rear position lamps shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

If the optional rear position lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1., the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, where the alternative geometric visibility is applied and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall be 45° outwards to 45° inwards, where the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane for a lamp mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.).

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, where the alternative geometric visibility is applied and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the vertical angle of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, where the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5° for a lamp mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.).

To be considered visible under the alternative geometric visibility, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps shall be provided, except when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamps shall be provided if required by the component Regulation.
The distance between the rear fog-lamp and each stop-lamp shall in all cases be greater than 100 mm.

The point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON, except that the rear position lamps may be switched OFF and remain switched OFF as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
The emergency stop signal shall be present on motor vehicles.
The emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the hazard warning signal is activated.

The angles of geometric visibility of each lamp, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The lamps shall not show red light towards the front or white light towards the rear, as checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.

Every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle shall function when switched on, in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
The tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps, as checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
